goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

The diff adds webhook secret envs (used for the *inbound* webhook) but does not use any shared secret for this *outbound* credential-sync call, so the receiving service has no built-in way to verify the caller from this request alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25 — Webhook secret is compared with !== rather than a constant-time comparison, exposing the shared secret to timing analysis

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the newly added authentication check compares the provided header value to the shared secret using `!==` (a normal string comparison): `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. This is not a constant-time comparison, so the review finding (timing side-channel risk for a shared secret comparison) is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:17 — Handler enforces no HTTP method, so GET/PUT/DELETE requests also reach the credential create/update path

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the exported Next.js API `handler` does not check `req.method` (e.g., `if (req.method !== "POST") return res.status(405)...`). As written, any HTTP method that passes the webhook-secret header check will proceed to `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` and then into the credential `update`/`create` paths. This exposes unintended behavior for PUT/DELETE/etc. (and GET may also reach parsing and throw).

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:58 — symmetricDecrypt is called with an empty-string key fallback when CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY is unset instead of failing closed with an explicit configuration error

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler, the decrypt call is `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")`, which does indeed fall back to an empty string when the env var is unset. However, the handler first checks `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) and returns 403 if it’s falsy, so the empty-key path should be unreachable when the key is truly unset. Still, using `|| ""` can mask misconfiguration and is worth tightening (e.g., throw/500 if missing) rather than silently substituting an empty key.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — schema.parse (line 31) and JSON.parse of the decrypted payload (line 57) are unguarded, so malformed or undecryptable input throws an unhandled exception and returns a 500 with error detail instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is called without a try/catch, so invalid input will throw a ZodError and bubble up as an unhandled exception (Next.js will return a 500). Similarly, `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` is unguarded; if decryption fails (e.g., wrong key/garbled ciphertext) or the decrypted string is not valid JSON, it will throw and also produce a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx response. This matches the finding and is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24 — No test covers the webhook secret comparison when CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET/header env vars are unset, where `undefined !== undefined` is false and the credential-writing endpoint authenticates anonymous callers.

adjudication.rationale: The handler gates the entire endpoint on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` (apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:16-19). That constant is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (packages/lib/constants.ts), so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset/undefined (or empty), the endpoint returns 403 before reaching the header comparison. Therefore the claimed `undefined !== undefined` bypass cannot occur from the shown diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31 — Malformed request bodies are untested: `schema.parse` throws rather than returning 400, so the handler's failure mode on bad input is unverified.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler calls `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` without a try/catch or use of `safeParse`. Zod's `parse` throws on invalid/malformed input, which in a Next.js API route will typically surface as an unhandled exception (500) rather than a controlled 400 response. This creates a broken/undesirable failure mode for bad request bodies introduced by this new endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57 — No test exercises symmetricDecrypt with the empty-string key fallback or JSON.parse of non-JSON plaintext, both of which throw out of the handler.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler calls `symmetricDecrypt(...)` and then `JSON.parse(...)` on the result without any try/catch. If the incoming `keys` ciphertext is invalid for the configured key (or decrypts to non-JSON), `symmetricDecrypt`/`JSON.parse` can throw and the request will bubble to a 500 rather than a controlled 4xx response. The finding’s “empty-string key fallback” is likely unreachable because `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is falsy when `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is empty, but the unhandled JSON/decrypt throw is still a real defect exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:72 — The update-existing vs create-new credential branches are untested, despite both writing arbitrary decrypted keys against a caller-supplied userId.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` with nontrivial branching behavior: it decrypts caller-provided `keys` and then either `prisma.credential.update(...)` or `prisma.credential.create(...)` based on `findFirst(...)` (the update vs create branches). No tests are added in this diff to cover these branches or validate the safety/expected behavior of persisting decrypted data keyed by a request-supplied `userId`/`appSlug` (even though access is gated by a shared secret header check). adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:15 — The two branches return different shapes (raw fetch Response vs whatever refreshFunction returns) and no test pins the contract callers depend on.

adjudication.rationale: `refreshOAuthTokens` returns fundamentally different runtime shapes depending on the branch: when credential sync is enabled it returns a raw `fetch(...)` `Response` (apps/webhook sync endpoint call), but otherwise it returns whatever `refreshFunction()` returns (often a parsed token object, or an axios/js client result). Call sites assume a specific shape: e.g. Google expects `res?.data` (`CalendarService.ts` assigns `const token = res?.data;`), Hubspot types the return as `HubspotToken` and will access token fields, etc. If `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, these callers would receive a `Response` instead of the expected object, causing broken refresh behavior at runtime. The finding about differing shapes is directly verifiable from `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts` and the shown usages.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:177 — The sharing-enabled path returns a fetch Response but the code treats it as a HubspotToken (`expiresIn`, `accessToken`); no test covers that path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts`, when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` it returns the result of `fetch(...)`, i.e. a `Response` object. In `packages/app-store/hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` assigns `const hubspotRefreshToken: HubspotToken = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. Under the sharing-enabled branch, `hubspotRefreshToken` will actually be a `Response`, but downstream Hubspot logic (not adjusted in this diff) expects a token-shaped object (per the `HubspotToken` type) and will break at runtime when accessing token fields. The 'no test covers that path' part isn’t verifiable from this diff, but the runtime type/behavior mismatch is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 — res?.data` assumes a Gaxios response; under credential sync refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response so `token` is undefined, and no test covers this branch.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `refreshAccessToken` now does `const res = await refreshOAuthTokens(...)` and then `const token = res?.data`. In the credential-sync branch, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the result of `fetch(...)` (`Response`), which does not have a `.data` property (unlike the Gaxios response from `myGoogleAuth.refreshToken(...).res`). This makes `token` undefined and leads to broken token refresh (`googleCredentials.access_token = token.access_token` etc.). The diff shows no handling of `Response.json()` for this branch, so the behavior is verifiably broken when `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` is set.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:100 — The persisted credential key is now the whole safeParse result (`{success, data}`) instead of the parsed keys, and no test asserts the stored credential shape.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the code changed from storing `googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials)` (the parsed credential object) to storing `parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)`. The new helper `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the Zod `safeParse` result object (`{ success, data, error }`), not `data` itself, and GoogleCalendarService persists that return value directly as `key` in `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key } })`. This would persist the wrong shape into the credential key field (including `success`/`data` wrapper), matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5 — minimumTokenResponseSchema's duplicate computed keys collapse into a single literal property, so it validates nothing about expiry; no test asserts what it accepts or rejects.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is built with two computed keys: `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()`. In a JS/TS object literal these computed keys evaluate to string literals (likely the same `toString()` value), so the latter overwrites the former. This does not implement the intended “any numeric property is expiry” validation and effectively fails to validate expiry fields as claimed. The comment about missing tests is not verifiable from the diff, but the schema construction itself is a concrete correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25 — The refresh_token defaulting to the literal string "refresh_token" is untested, yet that placeholder is written into stored credentials.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, if the parsed token payload lacks `refresh_token`, it is forcibly set to the literal string `"refresh_token"` (lines ~24-27). This value can then be persisted into credentials: e.g. in `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `tokenResponse = parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, ...)` is merged into `o365AuthCredentials` and then stored via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. Since many OAuth refresh responses omit `refresh_token`, this can overwrite a valid stored refresh token with the placeholder, breaking subsequent refreshes. The issue is directly verifiable from the diff regardless of test coverage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21 — Throwing instead of returning `success: false` changes error semantics and renders salesforce:92 and office365calendar:264 failure handling unreachable, shipped with no test.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the helper throws on `!refreshTokenResponse.success` (lines ~19-22) rather than returning a `SafeParseReturnType` with `success: false`. As a result, downstream checks for `!*.success` become unreachable, e.g. in `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` the code checks `if (!accessTokenParsed.success)` after calling `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...)`, but that branch can never execute because the function would have thrown earlier. Similarly, `office365calendar` now relies on a parse result that, by construction, will never be `success: false`. This is a real semantic change / inconsistency introduced by the diff, but whether throwing is incorrect vs. intended behavior isn't verifiable from the diff alone (and the claim about “no test” can’t be confirmed here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86 — The new unconditional refresh and its `response.statusText !== "OK"` gate are untested, so a runtime that returns an empty statusText would fail every getClient call undetected.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new refresh flow checks success via `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw ...` rather than `response.ok` / status code. This behavior is directly introduced by the diff.
